predecessors.name: Burgundians
predecessors.text: the Rhine settlement 'on the western bank of the Rhine', probably near Worms, with which Cliopatria's Burgundian Kingdom opens in 414

predecessors.name: Western Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the Rhine land ceded to the Burgundian foederati near Worms

successors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
successors.text: the whole kingdom: 'the rule of the Burgundian kings ended and the kingdom became part of Francia' in 534 (Kingdom page); 'definitively incorporated into their empire and finally divided among…

ledger.x: 413: the Burgundians become Roman foederati on the Rhine.
413: the Burgundians are Roman federates on the Rhine.
About 436: Aetius ends the federation.
About 436: Aetius and the Huns destroy the Rhine kingdom.
443: the survivors are settled in Sapaudia.
443: the capital is Geneva.
456: the Burgundians settle the Rhône valley.
458: Majorian takes Lyon.
461: the capital moves from Geneva to Lyon.
462: Lyon and the Rhône valley return to the Burgundians.
Mid-470s: the Burgundians push into the Alemannic marches.
500: Clovis and Godegisel fight Gundobad.
501: Gundobad retakes Vienne.
507: after Vouillé the Burgundians take Gothic Provence.
508: the Ostrogoths enter Provence.
509: the fighting ends on the Durance.
509: the Provence gains are lost.

Godomar II recovered territory south of the Durance during his reign: 'the recovery of territory south of the Durance', with no year and no bounds; after the victory of Vézeronce on 25 June 524 the Godomar page has 'With this army, he regained his territory'.
532: the Franks invade again.
534: the Burgundians are beaten near Autun.
534: the Franks end the Burgundian kingdom.

wars.name: Destruction of the Rhine kingdom by Aetius and the Huns
wars.outcome: Gundahar and many of his people were killed by Aetius working with his Hun allies; the survivors were settled in Sapaudia in 443.

wars.name: Majorian's Gallic campaign against the Burgundians
wars.outcome: Majorian defeated the Burgundians and besieged and conquered Lugdunum in late 458 or early 459; the city was fined and Sidonius Apollinaris delivered a panegyric in January 459.

wars.name: Burgundian war with the Visigoths on the lower Rhône
wars.outcome: Chilperic repelled a Visigothic move up the lower Rhône; no border moved.

wars.name: Burgundian campaigns against the Alemanni
wars.outcome: In the mid-470s the Burgundians took much of Maxima Sequanorum and parts of Lugdunensis I from the Alemanni.

wars.name: Burgundian invasion of Liguria
wars.outcome: While Odoacer and Theoderic fought over Pavia the Burgundians invaded northwestern Italy and devastated Liguria; no land was kept.

wars.name: Burgundian civil war and Clovis's intervention
wars.outcome: Gundobad lost near Dijon, fled to Avignon and was spared by Clovis for a yearly tribute; in 501 he besieged and killed Godegisel at Vienne and ended the tribute.

wars.name: Burgundian expansion in Provence and the Ostrogothic counter-offensive
wars.outcome: After Vouillé the Burgundians took Gothic land in Provence and besieged Arles; Ostrogothic forces relieved Arles and stripped the gains; the Durance became the southern frontier.

wars.name: Frankish-Burgundian war of 523-524
wars.outcome: Sigismund was captured and executed; his brother Godomar II defeated the Franks at Vézeronce on 25 June 524 ('On June 25, 524').

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Burgundy
wars.outcome: Godomar II could not repel the Franks; the defeat near Autun (534, Childebert I and Chlothar I) ended the kingdom, which the Franks divided among themselves.

certainty.note: The pages name cities, provinces and peoples (Worms, Sapaudia, Lyon, the Drôme, Provence), never a surveyed line.
